title: Introduce approval queue for elevated RBAC v2 grants with KMS usage attribution
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Customers asked for a transparent, auditable flow when service principals or operators request elevated RBAC v2 grants that also cause KMS key usage. Previously grants could be granted immediately by an admin or via automated policies which made compliance reviews and retroactive attribution hard. This PR introduces: 1) an approval queue service that records grant requests (who, why, TTL, requested roles, resource scope); 2) timebound provisional grants that can be auto-revoked after TTL if not escalated; 3) KMS usage attribution hooks so any KMS Encrypt/Decrypt/Sign operation performed while a provisional grant is active is annotated with an attestation token linking the KMS usage to the approval request; 4) an auditable hash chain persisted to the audit ledger topic to make tampering detectable; 5) a dual-signoff manual release flow in the Console for high-risk grants (requires two reviewers with distinct teams); and 6) migration tools to backfill existing short-lived grants into the queue to ensure consistent audit coverage. Checklist: - [x] Design doc: linear/ENG-5592 linked - [x] Approval queue service skeleton + API - [x] Console panel for reviewers with filtering by risk and region - [x] KMS attribution middleware and attestation token format - [x] Audit ledger hash-chain write + verification tool - [x] Dual-signoff UI and API gating - [x] E2E tests for provisional grant lifecycle - [x] Helm chart additions for deployment. Rollout plan: enabled by feature-flag (rbac.elevated_approval_queue) default off for existing clusters; opt-in per-tenant via Console or operator API. For Redwood Dedicated/Private, operators can enable in the installer values. Migration: a background migration scans for active grants created in the last 90 days and inserts them as "backfilled" requests with a small grace TTL; an operator must approve or reject backfilled items. Security considerations: attestation tokens are signed with the cluster KMS key and contain a minimal set of claims (request_id, principal, grant_scope, ttl, hash) to avoid leaking secrets. Audit ledger entries are append-only and include SHA256 over the canonical request blob; a verification utility is included to detect divergence. Backwards compatibility: the public inference API is unchanged; the RBAC decision point defers to approvals only for grants created via the new API path or flagged backfilled grants. Links: linear/ENG-5592, docs PR: docs/security/approval-queue.md, helm change: helm/charts/redwood/templates/approval-queue.yaml. Impact: expected slight latency increase for the initial grant path (synchronous persist + ledger write) but negligible for normal inference requests.

review_conversation: Lena Ortiz (reviewer): This looks solid; two concerns: (1) how do we ensure attestation token size doesn't escalate request headers, and (2) can we make the dual-signoff configurable per-tenant?

Author (Maya Chen): Attestation tokens are compacted and base64 url-safe; only the request_id is propagated in headers to keep per-request overhead minimal. Dual-signoff is gated by tenant feature flags and a cluster policy; updated docs include opt-in instructions.
Daniel Park (reviewer): Security scan reported a high entropy key usage pattern in tests — can we avoid committing test keys?
Author (Maya Chen): Removed embedded test keys and added mock signer interface; CI now runs with in-memory signer for unit tests and a dedicated test KMS instance for integration runs.
Priya Reddy (approver): Approving pending the small nit around log verbosity in the approval_queue worker.
release_notes: New feature: Approval Queue for elevated RBAC grants with KMS usage attribution. Adds an auditable provisional grant flow, dual-signoff manual release, and migration/backfill tooling. Feature gated behind rbac.elevated_approval_queue. No breaking API changes.
notes_for_ops: For Dedicated/Private deployments: add 'approvalQueue.enabled=true' to helm values, ensure the cluster KMS key has sign permission for attestation tokens, and schedule the backfill job during a maintenance window. The ledger verifier should be run weekly as a cronjob.
post_merge_tasks: (1) enable feature-flag rollout to staging; (2) run migration backfill on staging and collect metrics; (3) widen canary to 5% of tenants; (4) onboard compliance team with verifier guide in docs/security/approval-queue.md
